_note: Level 1 functional flow: the team's nine blocks (Acquire, Transmit, Process, Evaluate, Generate, Broadcast, Receive, Verify, Coordinate) with their sub-steps. F1-F8 run in sequence; at F8, missing acknowledgments send the alert back to F6; F9 Coordinate is persistent and runs alongside the others. Latency allocations and derived L1 requirements are DRAFTS for the team to adjust; the team's own requirements take precedence.

hazards.name: Flooding
hazards.detect_example: River gauge reads water rising past its alert level

hazards.name: Fire
hazards.detect_example: Smoke sensor in the savanna belt trips; satellite hotspot from another system confirms

hazards.name: Illegal logging / deforestation
hazards.detect_example: Acoustic sensor hears a chainsaw; S-2 radar shows new canopy loss

hazards.name: Illegal mining / pollution
hazards.detect_example: Water-quality probe sees a turbidity spike below a mining zone

hazards.name: Wildlife and poaching
hazards.detect_example: Tagged elephant stops moving, or a gunshot is detected

hazards.name: Disease and community emergencies
hazards.detect_example: Ranger or health worker sends a priority report from a handheld

functions.name: Acquire
functions.title: Acquire Environment & Field Data
functions.description: A sensor, tag, ranger device or partner system measures conditions, adds observation metadata, formats a standardized message, sets its priority and queues it for transmission.
functions.outputs: Prioritized, standardized message (a few hundred bytes), queued

functions.name: Transmit
functions.title: Transmit Data to Ground
functions.description: The terminal picks an available satellite path and links up (directly, through its raised antenna, or through a station or repeater under canopy); the satellite receives and validates the message, directs it to the right ground terminal and forwards it to the ground system, and reception is acknowledged.
steps: Direct message towards correct ground terminal
functions.outputs: Message at the ground system; reception acknowledged

functions.name: Process
functions.title: Process Data
functions.description: The regional database receives and validates the message, reconciles it with existing records, stores it, updates the current models and distributes the information to the monitors in the common operating picture.
steps: Reconcile incoming observations with existing records
functions.outputs: Validated record in the COP; models updated

functions.name: Evaluate
functions.title: Evaluate Conditions
functions.description: Relevant data is retrieved, measurements are compared with thresholds and correlated across sources, hazard severity and location are assessed, and the agencies decide whether an alert is needed.
steps: Correlate observations of multiple data sources
performed_by: Partner systems (for example an S-1 revisit)
functions.outputs: Hazard severity and location; alert decision

functions.name: Generate
functions.title: Generate Alerts
functions.description: A proposed alert is generated, checked against its source data, customized for the geographic location of the hazard and completed as a full alert message, under the national alerting authority.
steps: Validate alert information and source data
Customize alert for geographic location of hazard

latency_min.budget: outside S-3 timing (agency decision); the S3-05 clock starts when the authorized alert reaches S-3

functions.name: Broadcast
functions.title: Broadcast Alerts
functions.description: S-3 identifies the target recipients and the pathway, sends the alert from the ground system to the satellite network, relays it across the network and delivers it to community receivers and responders, then reports delivery status.
steps: Transmit alert from ground system to satellite network
Deliver alert to community receivers and responders

functions.name: Receive
functions.title: Receive & Present Alerts
functions.description: The receiver or terminal receives and validates the alert, converts text to spoken audio if required, activates the community notification interface or presents it on the terminal, records reception and transmits an acknowledgement.
steps: Receive alert on receiver or terminal
Convert alert text into spoken audio if required

functions.name: Verify
functions.title: Verify
functions.description: Delivery acknowledgments come back and the alert delivery status is updated; missing acknowledgments are identified, satellite and terminal health is inspected and operators are told of any degradation. If acknowledgments are missing, the alert goes back to F6 and is broadcast again to the receivers that have not answered.
steps: Notify operators of degradation if necessary

decision.question: All targeted receivers acknowledged?
decision.no_label: Rebroadcast to receivers that have not acknowledged

functions.name: Coordinate
functions.title: Coordinate Response
functions.description: Runs alongside every other block: responders message in, are authenticated and prioritized; messages go through the satellite network and are delivered to the outposts; return commands and messages are relayed; field reports update the models; communication queues are maintained. Works with towers and the grid down.
steps: Update models with relevant field reports
performed_by: LEO satellites; A-1 relay as a complement
functions.outputs: Commands and messages delivered; field reports into the models

S3-09.note: per message (an acknowledgment in F8, a command in F9), not a sum

derived_L1_drafts.text: The system shall receive messages from terminals anywhere within the basin boundary, including terminals under 30-40 m canopy within relay range of a ranger station.
The space segment shall provide a satellite in simultaneous view of an open-sky terminal and a gateway within 18 min at the 95th percentile (threshold) and 2.5 min (objective).
The ground segment shall deliver a downlinked priority message to the hub COP within 10 min (threshold) and 2 min (objective) at >= 95% / >= 99% completeness.
Every database node shall hold a full replica and shall be able to run F3-F8 alone if the hub is unreachable.
The hub shall convert an authorized CAP alert into geo-targeted speech and put it on air within 4 min (threshold) and 1.25 min (objective).
The broadcast shall address areas of <= 50,000 km2 (threshold) / <= 2,500 km2 (objective) and carry French, Lingala, Kiswahili, Kikongo and Tshiluba.
Community receivers in the target area shall play the alert aloud within 6 min of broadcast (threshold), 1.75 min (objective), for >= 95% / >= 99% of receivers.
The community receiver shall cost <= $25, run from solar or hand crank, and receive with a fixed antenna needing no pointing.
Each ranger station shall return a delivery confirmation for its area within 6 h (threshold) and 15 min (objective).
The system shall support >= 500 simultaneous responder terminals at >= 4.8 kbps with all terrestrial networks down.
Ranger stations shall keep alerting and two-way service through 5 days without sun, using storage, micro-hydro where available, and hand crank.
No alert shall be broadcast without a valid CAP message signed by an authorized national agency.
